title: An Afternoon in Esplanade
excerpt: A familiar part of the city, a few market stalls, and a walk with no particular hurry.
opening: I pass through Esplanade quite often. When I carry my camera, I stop at the shops instead of walking straight past. Most of these photographs show the people working there. I don’t go there with a fixed list of pictures to take. I look at the counters and shopfronts, then decide where I want to stop. There is a lot to look at even along a short stretch of shops. I tend to spend time with one stall before turning the camera towards the next one.

The stalls are close together, and there is always something in front of the camera. I left some of that in the photographs: a shopper’s shoulder, hanging packets, and the goods around each shopkeeper. I could have moved closer and cut out more of the street, but that would leave out much of what I was looking at. I wanted the shops to look as busy as they were. Some of the shopkeepers are easy to see behind their counters. Others sit among so many things for sale that I notice their faces only after looking through the rest of the picture.
ending: I kept these photographs together because they show the shops, the people and the things I noticed on this walk. I don’t have one explanation for all of them. Some are about the people, while others are simply things I wanted to take a closer look at.

cover.alt: Two women browse colourful accessories at a market stall in front of a closed metal shutter.
cover.caption: Seller at closed shutter

images.alt: A seated vendor looks out from shelves of sweets and small goods, framed by a shopper’s blue shoulder and bright packets overhead.
images.caption: Behind the crowded counter
images.note: I noticed the vendor behind the shelves first. The shopper in front blocks part of the view, but I kept that in the photograph. It shows how crowded the shop was. The light over the counter makes the goods much brighter than the space behind them. I still notice the man’s face first, then start looking through the rest of the stall.

images.alt: A shopkeeper leans over plush toys as a child reaches in; red hearts and crowded shelves turn the stall into a scene.
images.caption: Seller and his toys
images.note: The toy stall has colour almost everywhere. I wanted to include the shopkeeper as well as the toys, even though there was very little room around him. The people in front cover part of the display. I left them there because they show the shop being used, rather than just a wall of toys. The shopkeeper has almost as much around his head as the children do.

images.alt: A woman in a black veil meets the camera among several shoppers, the faces and patterned shawls filling the crowded street view.
images.caption: Faces between market stalls
images.note: People fill most of this photograph. I kept it because of the faces looking in different directions, especially the woman looking towards the camera. There are patterned clothes, shoppers and parts of several stalls close together. I didn’t want to crop out all of that. The woman’s face is clear enough to notice even with so much around her.

images.alt: A vendor leans over his produce while two men sort fruit, their faces framed by hanging goods and the stall’s warm light.
images.caption: At the fruit stall
images.note: At the fruit stall, I watched the men working around the produce. The hanging goods and warm light were part of what caught my attention. The men are looking down at what they are doing rather than towards me. I like that about this photograph. The work at the stall matters as much as the faces.

images.alt: Desk fans line the shop display in repeated circles of pink, yellow and mint, their glossy plastic catching the warm lights overhead.
images.caption: Colourful fans for sale
images.note: I also photographed this display of fans. I liked the colours and the repeated circles. Not every picture from the walk needed to include a person. The pink, yellow and green plastic looks different from the shelves and shopfronts in the other pictures. I kept a fairly close view so the repeated shapes would be easy to see.

quote: Sometimes I take the long way without really meaning to.

title: A Few Days in the Hills
excerpt: Water through the trees, houses on the slopes, and clouds that keep changing the view.
opening: I took these photographs in Sikkim. The clouds kept changing what I could see, so I often looked at the same hillside more than once before moving on. Sometimes I could see the houses on the next slope, and sometimes cloud covered most of them. I took a few versions instead of assuming the first photograph would be the one I kept. The closer slopes stayed fairly clear, while the more distant ones came in and out of view. I tried to include enough of the nearer trees and houses to show that difference.

I photographed the waterfalls and the wider views, but I also stopped for houses, roadside scenes and flowers. This set includes a few of each. I don’t want every photograph from a trip to be a wide landscape. The smaller subjects help me remember what I looked at between those bigger views. The houses show how people use the steep slopes, and the road pictures show a different part of the place. I like being able to look at those alongside the waterfalls.
ending: These are my picks from this part of the trip. I prefer looking at a few pictures at a time rather than putting the whole folder on one page. It makes it easier to notice the differences between them. I can always come back to the photographs later and choose another set.

cover.alt: A waterfall pours down a rocky slope through dense greenery, with branches framing the white stream against the dark hillside.
cover.caption: Waterfall through the green forest

images.alt: Colourful homes cling to the steep hillside beneath soft cloud, while the green valley fades toward a blue-grey mountain line.
images.caption: A hillside town
images.note: I liked the coloured houses against the green hillside. They also give me a better idea of the size of the hills than a photograph of the slopes alone. There are roofs at several heights, with more slopes behind them. I kept the wider view because it shows how the town sits on the hillside, rather than showing just a few buildings.

images.alt: A bus follows the narrow hillside road into drifting mist, with wet rock and dense forest closing around its route.
images.caption: The bus through mountain fog
images.note: The bus was the first thing I noticed on this road. The mist hides much of what lies ahead, but I can still follow the road through the photograph. The wet rock and trees take up much of the picture. I didn’t try to make the road look wider or more open. The bus gives me something clear to look at in the middle of all that mist.

images.alt: Yellow and violet blossoms catch a narrow beam above broad dark leaves, isolated from the surrounding forest by the shallow focus.
images.caption: Flower against forest floor
images.note: I stopped for these flowers as well. After taking several photographs of distant hills, I wanted to look at something closer to me. The yellow and violet stand out against the darker leaves. I kept the surrounding ground quite dark, so the flowers remain the first thing I see when I look back at the picture.

images.alt: Water drops between dark rocks, cutting a bright line through the monochrome forest and falling toward the shadowed valley floor.
images.caption: Waterfall through dark pines
images.note: I kept this waterfall photograph in black and white. Without the green around it, I notice the white water and the dark trees first. There is still plenty of detail around the stream. Some branches cross in front of it, and the rocks break up the water below. I wanted to keep those parts instead of making a picture of the water alone.

images.alt: A hillside town glitters against the night, each cluster of lights tracing the slope beneath the deep, nearly black sky.
images.caption: Gangtok scattered across the dark
images.note: At night, I photographed the lights across the hillside. The windows and roads make the shape of the town easier to see against the dark slopes. Large parts of the hill are unlit. I left those dark areas in the picture because they show how far the lights spread, and where the buildings become difficult to make out.

quote: I stopped for the smaller things as well as the view.

title: The Flower Market, Before Noon
excerpt: People around the stalls, piles of leaves, and the work going on between the flowers.
opening: At the flower market, I photograph more than the flowers. I notice the people sorting goods, waiting at their stalls and making their way through the narrow lanes. There is often more happening at the edge of a stall than in the display itself. I look around the people as well as at them, especially when several jobs are happening in the same small space. The tables are close together and the walkways are busy. Sometimes the part that interests me is a person working behind the display, rather than the things laid out in front.

These photographs include those parts of the market too. I kept the tables, doorways and people around the main subject because I wanted to show where I was standing. The pictures can get crowded, and I don’t always find a clear view. I try to keep enough of the surroundings to make sense of the scene without losing the person I noticed first. I also pay attention to the quieter parts of a stall. Someone sitting beside a doorway or waiting at a counter can hold my attention just as much as a group at work.
ending: I kept this set because it includes the work around the market as well as the stalls themselves. That is what I spent most of my time photographing. I also wanted to keep a few things I hadn’t gone there expecting to photograph, including the dog and the quieter moments beside the counters.

cover.alt: A woman reaches into a pile of greens, her red sari arcing across the frame above the bed of leaves.
cover.caption: Gathering green leaves from the stall

images.alt: Several men lean over a market table, sorting items while their checked shirts and close shoulders form a busy cluster.
images.caption: Vendors gathered around the market goods
images.note: Several people were working around this table. I liked how they leaned in from different sides, with their hands and shoulders close together. I can follow what each person is doing without seeing everyone’s face clearly. The checked shirts and the edge of the table also help me separate the people from one another.

images.alt: The vendor waits behind his counter as a woman passes in profile; hanging pictures and stacked produce gather around him.
images.caption: A pause at the fruit stall
images.note: This vendor was waiting behind his counter while someone passed in front. I kept this photograph alongside the busier scenes from the market. The things hanging behind him and the goods on the counter fill most of the space. I included the person passing because I liked seeing both parts of the scene in the same picture.

images.alt: An older man sits in the shadowed stall, his turquoise trousers against the quiet clutter and black doorway around him.
images.caption: Seated shopkeeper in the blue light
images.note: The man’s blue trousers caught my attention. I then noticed the dark doorway behind him and the things around the stall, so I included those as well. The blue is one of the few strong colours in this part of the stall. It helped me notice the seated man before I started looking at the smaller things in the shadows.

images.alt: A white dog walks past a seated man and standing vendors beside a metal gate on the paved market lane.
images.caption: A dog beside the market entrance
images.note: I photographed the dog passing the people beside the gate. It was something else I noticed while walking through the market, away from the tables of goods. The dog is easy to pick out against the darker gate and clothing. I also liked the space between the seated man and the people standing nearby. I didn’t need a closer view for the picture to work.

images.alt: A worker bends over a basin in the wet street, beside buckets, scattered produce and dim market stalls behind him.
images.caption: Water work in the market lane
images.note: I included more of the wet lane in this photograph. I wanted to show the buckets and the work going on around the stalls, rather than crop in on the person. The ground takes up a good part of the picture, with the person bending down beside the containers. That tells me more about the work than a close photograph of a face would.

quote: I spent more time watching the people than the flowers.

title: I Took the Long Way Home
excerpt: A few photographs by the river, where there is always a reason to wait a little longer.
opening: I often take the longer way home when I have my camera. Sometimes that takes me to the river, where I stop to photograph the bridge, the boats and the people along the bank. I don’t always take many pictures when I stop there. Sometimes I wait and look around, especially when the light is changing and people are moving along the bank. There are people sitting near the water, others standing at the railings, and boats moving further out. I look around those smaller subjects before deciding how much of the bridge to include.

For these pictures, I wanted the bridge in the frame without making it the only subject. I also looked for people near the water and the changing light behind them. I tried a few wider and closer views. In some pictures, the people are easy to pick out. In others, they are small shapes beneath the bridge. Keeping several views from the same walk lets me compare them afterwards. A small change in where I stand can change which person, cable or patch of sky I notice first.
ending: These are the photographs I kept from that walk. I took longer to get home, but I was happy to spend the extra time by the river. I like having a few different views from the same place. When I look through them together, I can see how much the light changed while I was there.

cover.alt: A narrow boat travels beneath a streaked orange horizon, its dark outline separating the bright band of clouded sky from the broad river.
cover.caption: Last light over the water

images.alt: Two figures sit low beside the river as the bridge spans the glowing dusk, their dark silhouettes held against water and orange sky.
images.caption: A couple beneath the bridge
images.note: I included the two people sitting by the water as well as the bridge. I like having someone in the foreground when I photograph a view this wide. They give me a way to judge the distance across the water. I left some room around them so they would remain part of the view instead of turning the picture into a close portrait.

images.alt: Silhouettes stand at the river’s edge beneath the steel bridge, framed by a thin orange sunset and the broader band of dark water.
images.caption: Two figures at bridge railing
images.note: There was only a narrow band of orange left above the river. I kept the figures and the dark water in the frame instead of taking a closer photograph of the sky. The silhouettes are still clear against that thin bit of colour. I liked that I could include so much dark water and still tell where the people were standing.

images.alt: Blue hour settles over the bridge while blurred visitors gather along the bank, their movement softened against the crisp lights and dark water.
images.caption: Bridge above the river crowd
images.note: More people gathered along this part of the bank. I wanted to include the crowd beneath the bridge rather than try to find an empty view. Some figures overlap and are difficult to separate. I left that in because I was interested in how people gathered along the bank, not in making a portrait of each person.

images.alt: The cable bridge cuts diagonally across the blue river, its illuminated span mirrored in broken streaks below as the darkening sky gathers overhead.
images.caption: Bridge cables over evening water
images.note: I tried a few positions for this photograph. I was looking at how the bridge cables lined up with the river and the people near the edge. Moving a little changes how much of the steel structure crosses the sky. I kept trying until I found a view where I could still see the people and the water below it.

images.alt: Buildings glow across the broad river beneath a deep blue sky, their broken reflections gathering in long bands on the dark water.
images.caption: Waterfront lights at blue hour
images.note: I stayed until the lights across the water became easier to see. By then, I was taking fewer pictures and spending more time looking at the river. The bright points on the far bank show up against the blue water, while much of the bridge stays dark. I wanted to keep both in the picture instead of cropping down to the lights.

quote: I usually stay by the river longer than I plan to.

title: A Walk Through Delhi
excerpt: Red sandstone, shaded gateways and the people passing through, from Humayun’s Tomb to Qutub Minar.
opening: I took these photographs around Humayun’s Tomb and Qutub Minar in Delhi. I was looking at the buildings, but I kept noticing the things around them as well: trees across a view, people moving through an entrance, and a reflection close to the ground. I wanted to keep those parts in the photographs. They gave me a few different ways to look at the same place without always standing directly in front of it.

Some of the pictures are in colour, with red stone against the sky or the warm light on the tower after dark. Others are in black and white. In those, I was more interested in the shape of an arch, the shade under the trees and the people crossing the path. I’ve put them together here because I like seeing the wider views beside the closer, busier ones. The buildings stay recognisable, even when they are only part of the frame.
ending: I’ve kept this selection small: a reflection, a few gateways, people walking and the tower at the end. Looking through the photographs, I spend as much time on the trees and passing figures as I do on the stonework. Those are the parts that made each view different for me. I like having them in the frame alongside the buildings.

cover.alt: The red sandstone tomb appears upside down in the pool, its arches and palms softened by ripples across the foreground water.
cover.caption: Pool reflection

images.alt: A red sandstone gateway with a central arch, pale decorative edges and small domed roofs beneath a blue sky.
images.caption: At the red gateway
images.note: I photographed the red gateway almost straight on. The main arch is easy to find, but there are smaller openings, pale edges and domed roofs around it. I left enough room above the building for the sky. I liked being able to look across the whole façade instead of concentrating only on the entrance.

images.alt: In monochrome, the garden gate frames a smaller arch beyond it; branches and deep shade enclose the path to the tomb.
images.caption: Through the shaded gateway
images.note: The trees make this gateway feel quite different from the first one. I kept the branches and the darker garden around the stonework rather than cropping them away. The openings line up through the middle, with the courtyard and path visible beyond. In black and white, I notice those repeated shapes before the smaller details.

images.alt: Blurred visitors cross a garden path between dark trees, with a stone gateway visible in the distance.
images.caption: Passing through the garden
images.note: People pass close to the camera in this photograph, while the garden path and gateway stay clear behind them. I kept the movement instead of waiting for an empty view. Some of the figures overlap and blur together. I like how that changes a fairly straight view down the path into something with people moving through it.

images.alt: Qutub Minar rises between dark trees in monochrome, its carved stone bands and narrow balconies sharply defined against the open sky above.
images.caption: Qutub Minar between the trees
images.note: I looked at Qutub Minar through the trees for this picture. The branches cover some of the lower structure, leaving the tower visible against the brighter sky. I wanted to keep that dark frame around it. In black and white, the shape of the tower stays clear without losing the leaves and smaller branches at the edges.

images.alt: The lit tower stands beyond old stone walls, its amber details rising sharply against the deep blue evening sky.
images.caption: The tower after dark
images.note: I’ve ended with the tower lit against a deep blue sky. Part of the old stone wall remains on the left, with a few visitors low in the frame. I kept those darker shapes in the picture instead of showing only the illuminated tower. The warmer stone and the blue sky are what I notice first when I come back to this photograph.

quote: I kept looking at what was around the monuments.

title: Another Day in Kolkata
excerpt: Workshop doors, unfinished figures and the ordinary things that make me stop with the camera.
opening: I took these photographs in Kumartuli and other parts of Kolkata. I usually walk around without a list of things to photograph. I stop when I notice a person, a workshop or something happening nearby. I often notice what is around a person before I decide where to stand. A doorway, a stack of goods or part of a figure can make me look at the scene for longer. The camera gives me a reason to pay closer attention to places I might otherwise walk past. I don’t need to find a new subject every time I go out.

In Kumartuli, I looked at the people working among the clay figures. I wanted to include the rooms around them, as well as a few closer views of the work. The unfinished figures can take up nearly the whole view. I look for a place where I can still see the people and what they are doing among all of that work. Some pictures include most of the room, while others concentrate on the person and the figure in front of them. Looking at both helps me show the workshop without repeating the same view.
ending: I’ve put the workshop and street photographs together because this is how I usually take pictures: I walk around and stop when I see something I want to photograph. The subjects don’t have to match exactly. I’m more interested in keeping the pictures I spent time looking at, whether I took them in a workshop, beside a shop or down by the water.

cover.alt: A bespectacled artisan leans toward the soft clay portrait, his cheek and the unfinished statue’s smooth profile catching the same warm light.
cover.caption: A sculptor beside model’s face

images.alt: Two workers lean toward a clay figure in the busy studio, surrounded by unfinished statues and carved forms beneath the crowded roof.
images.caption: Two workers among unfinished figures
images.note: I left the unfinished figures around the workers in this photograph. They show how much was happening inside the room and how little space the people had to work in. The figures are at different stages, and there are pieces of work in front of and behind the men. A closer crop would lose much of that, so I kept more of the workshop in view.

images.alt: Several clay arms reach inward around a small sculpted face, creating a crowded workshop view where one bright eye holds the centre.
images.caption: Hands among unfinished clay figures
images.note: The clay hands surround a small face in this picture. I kept it in black and white so I could see the shapes clearly against the darker workshop. Some of the hands overlap, while others point in different directions. I liked looking through them towards the face. It took me longer to notice the smaller details around the edges.

images.alt: A seated artisan studies a soft clay head at close range, his profile surrounded by shelves of miniature figures and workshop tools.
images.caption: The sculptor among small faces
images.note: For this closer view, I focused on the sculptor and the head in front of him. The shelves of smaller figures still show part of the room around him. The person’s profile and the clay head are close together. I wanted to show both clearly, while leaving enough of the shelves to make it clear that he was inside a busy workshop.

images.alt: A man sits outside the lowered shutter with small goods arranged beside him, his white shirt catching the shop’s soft warm light.
images.caption: A vendor in blue
images.note: Away from the workshops, I noticed this man beside a closed shutter. I included the goods next to him and the light falling on his shirt. It is a different subject from the clay figures, but I still looked at the space around the person. The shutter and the small display beside him were important parts of the picture for me.

images.alt: Several people stand in silhouette beneath the steel span, looking toward the broad river as the last orange light thins across the horizon.
images.caption: Watching the bridge at dusk
images.note: I’ve ended this set with the people looking across the river. I wanted the bridge, the water and the last colour in the sky in the same photograph. The people are small against the steel structure. I left the view wide because I wanted to show them standing there together, rather than pick out just one person from the group.

quote: I usually go out without a list of things to photograph.
